Subject: [unmarked] colext error in data.frame(..., check.names=FALSE): arguments imply differing number of rows

Hi,
After reading the colext vignette and listening to the webinar, I started in on my own data, but I'm running into an error message that I can't figure out. 
I have a dataframe that is similar to the ALFL0506 data and I set up my umf as follows
VA.y <- VA.data[,2:32]
VA.y[VA.y>1] <- 1
VA.umf <- unmarkedMultFrame(y=VA.y,
                            siteCovs=VA.data[,128:129],                                  
                            obsCovs=list(temp=VA.data[,64:94],
                                           wind=VA.data[,95:125]),
                              numPrimary=10)
My umf checks out fine but when I run models
(fm1 <- colext(~1, ~1, ~1, ~1, VA.umf))
I get this error message:
Error in data.frame(..., check.names = FALSE) : 
  arguments imply differing number of rows: 3100, 3000
I did some searching and further reading but was unable to figure out what this error message means or how to fix it.
Any ideas what is going wrong?
Thanks much for your help!
-Kathi

messages.author: 4a15de51da4445ae
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] colext error in data.frame(..., check.names=FALSE): arguments imply differing number of rows
parts:
hi Kathi,
 it seems like you have a different missing data pattern for the covariates and I bet thats causing the problem.
 To check that, please fill-in all of the NA values with any reasonable number (the mean value) and make sure it works.
 But it is a definite problem if you have so much missing data.
andy

messages.author: df74d6fccec2ff7e
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] colext error in data.frame(..., check.names=FALSE): arguments imply differing number of rows
parts:
Hi Kathi,

I think the problem is that your "y" matrix has 31 columns but numPrimary=10. It looks like this is due to the fact that you had 3 secondary sampling occasions in some years and 4 in others. To fix this, just add a column of NAs to the years with only 3 occasions. I will try to add a better error message.

Richard
